subject: Theory of Computation, Computer Graphics, Java/Web & Advanced Algorithms
exam_relevance: 10-12 questions expected in BPSC TRE CS exam

questions.question: Which mathematical model is the simplest automaton that recognizes regular languages?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Finite Automata (DFA and NFA) recognize exactly the class of Regular Languages (Type-3 in Chomsky hierarchy).

questions.question: In a Deterministic Finite Automaton (DFA), for every state and input symbol there is:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In a DFA, the transition function δ: Q × Σ → Q maps each state and input symbol to exactly one next state, with no ε-transitions.

questions.question: If an NFA has n states, what is the maximum number of states in an equivalent DFA?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: By subset construction, an n-state NFA can be converted into an equivalent DFA with at most 2^n states.

questions.question: Which statement holds true regarding the expressive power of DFA, NFA, and ε-NFA?

options.B: Every NFA has an equivalent DFA
options.C: Every ε-NFA has an equivalent NFA
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: DFA, NFA, and ε-NFA are equivalent in power and recognize exactly the regular languages. All three statements A, B, and C are true.

questions.question: Which regular expression denotes the set of all binary strings over {0, 1} ending with '01'?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: (0+1)* generates any prefix of 0s and 1s, followed by the mandatory suffix '01'.

questions.question: The Pumping Lemma for regular languages is primarily used to:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Pumping Lemma is a necessary (not sufficient) condition used to prove that a language is NOT regular, not to prove regularity.

questions.question: Which of the following languages is NOT regular?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: L = { a^n b^n | n >= 0 } requires unbounded counting/memory to match a's and b's, so it is context-free but not regular.

questions.question: Which data structure provides auxiliary memory to a Pushdown Automaton (PDA)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A Pushdown Automaton extends a finite automaton with an unbounded LIFO stack, enabling it to recognize context-free languages.

questions.question: Context-Free Grammars (CFGs) are recognized by which class of automata?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Non-deterministic Pushdown Automata (NPDA) recognize all Context-Free Languages; DPDA recognizes only deterministic CFLs.

questions.question: In Chomsky Normal Form (CNF), every production rule (except S → ε) has the form:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In CNF, productions are A → BC (two variables) or A → a (single terminal), plus optionally S → ε. Thus both A and B are valid.

questions.question: A Context-Free Grammar is called ambiguous if:

options.A: Some string has two parse trees
options.C: It has more than one variable
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A CFG is ambiguous if at least one string in its language has two or more distinct parse trees (or leftmost derivations).

questions.question: According to the Chomsky Hierarchy, Type-2 grammars correspond to:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Chomsky Hierarchy: Type-0 Unrestricted, Type-1 Context-Sensitive, Type-2 Context-Free, Type-3 Regular.

questions.question: Which automaton recognizes Type-1 (Context-Sensitive) languages in the Chomsky Hierarchy?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A Linear Bounded Automaton (LBA) is a restricted Turing Machine whose tape is bounded by a linear function of input length.

questions.question: The class of languages accepted by Turing Machines is known as:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Turing Machines recognize Recursively Enumerable (Type-0) languages, where the machine halts and accepts strings in the language.

questions.question: What does the Halting Problem prove about Turing Machines?

options.A: It is solvable in polynomial time
options.B: It is undecidable by any algorithm
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Alan Turing proved in 1936 that no general algorithm can decide for every TM and input whether the TM eventually halts.

questions.question: Which problem is decidable for Deterministic Finite Automata (DFA)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Membership, emptiness, finiteness, and equivalence are all decidable for DFAs. All three statements A, B, and C are decidable.

questions.question: Regular languages are closed under which of the following operations?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Regular languages are closed under intersection and complement (as well as finite union), but not under infinite union or arbitrary subsets.

questions.question: Context-Free Languages are NOT closed under which operation?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: CFLs ARE closed under union, concatenation, and Kleene star; they are NOT closed under intersection and complementation.

questions.question: In a Mealy machine, the output depends on:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In a Mealy machine, output is a function of both current state and current input; in a Moore machine, it depends only on current state.

questions.question: Which theorem states that finite automata and regular expressions have identical expressive power?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Kleene's theorem establishes that a language is accepted by a finite automaton if and only if it is described by a regular expression.

questions.question: How does a multi-tape Turing Machine compare in computational power to a single-tape Turing Machine?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Every multi-tape Turing Machine can be simulated by a single-tape Turing Machine, so both recognize the exact same class of languages.

questions.question: Which thesis states that any effectively computable function can be computed by a Turing Machine?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Church-Turing Thesis asserts that intuitive algorithmic computability is equivalent to Turing Machine computability.

questions.question: Which problem is UNDECIDABLE for general Context-Free Grammars?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Membership (via CYK), emptiness, and finiteness are all decidable for CFGs; ambiguity and equivalence of CFGs are undecidable.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of states in a DFA accepting all strings over {0,1} whose length is divisible by 3?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: States track length mod 3 (remainders 0, 1, 2), requiring 3 states, with remainder 0 as both initial and accepting state.

questions.question: In a Turing Machine transition δ(q, a) = (p, b, R), what does 'R' indicate?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In δ(q, a) = (p, b, R), the TM switches to state p, writes symbol b, and moves the read/write head one cell to the Right (R).

questions.question: In raster-scan displays, the electron beam sweeps across the screen:

options.B: From top to bottom row by row
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A raster-scan CRT sweeps the electron beam horizontally across each scan line from top to bottom, illuminating pixels stored in the frame buffer.

questions.question: Random-scan (vector) displays are primarily suited for:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Random-scan displays direct the electron beam only to parts where a picture is drawn, making them ideal for crisp line drawings and CAD.

questions.question: How much memory is required for a 1024 × 768 frame buffer with 24 bits per pixel (true color)?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.question: Why is Bresenham's line algorithm preferred over the DDA algorithm?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Bresenham's algorithm uses only integer addition, subtraction, and bit shifts, avoiding slow floating-point math and rounding in DDA.

questions.question: In the DDA line-drawing algorithm for a line with slope |m| <= 1 (x1 < x2), each step increments:

options.A: x by 1 and y by m
options.B: y by 1 and x by m
options.C: x by m and y by 1/m
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: When |m| <= 1, x is sampled at unit intervals (Δx = 1) and y increases by m = Δy/Δx at each step.

questions.question: In the Midpoint Circle algorithm, symmetry reduces computation from 8 octants to:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Because a circle has 8-way symmetry, computing points in one 45-degree octant yields all 8 symmetric points around the center.

questions.question: In the Cohen-Sutherland 2D line clipping algorithm, each endpoint is assigned a:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Cohen-Sutherland divides 2D space into 9 regions using a 4-bit outcode (Top, Bottom, Right, Left = TBRL).

questions.question: In Cohen-Sutherland clipping, a line segment is trivially ACCEPTED if:

options.A: Bitwise AND of codes is non-zero
options.B: Bitwise OR of both codes is 0000
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: If both endpoint region codes are 0000 (bitwise OR = 0000), both endpoints lie inside the clipping window, so the line is trivially accepted.

questions.question: Why are homogeneous coordinates (3×3 matrices for 2D) used in geometric transformations?

options.A: To represent translation via matrix multiplication
options.C: To combine scaling and rotation with translation
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Homogeneous coordinates turn translation into matrix multiplication, allowing translation, rotation, and scaling to be composed into one matrix.

questions.question: In 2D graphics, rotating a point (x, y) counter-clockwise by angle θ around the origin produces:

options.A: (x cosθ - y sinθ, x sinθ + y cosθ)
options.B: (x cosθ + y sinθ, x sinθ - y cosθ)
options.C: (x sinθ - y cosθ, x cosθ + y sinθ)
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Standard 2D counter-clockwise rotation matrix gives x' = x cosθ - y sinθ and y' = x sinθ + y cosθ.

questions.question: Reflection of a 2D point (x, y) across the X-axis yields:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Reflecting across the X-axis keeps the x-coordinate unchanged and negates the y-coordinate: (x, -y).

questions.question: Which 2D transformation changes the shape of an object by shifting coordinates proportionally to another axis?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Shearing distorts an object's shape (e.g., turning a rectangle into a parallelogram) by shifting one coordinate proportional to the other.

questions.question: Which projection preserves relative proportions and parallel lines without foreshortening by distance?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Parallel (orthographic/oblique) projection preserves parallel lines and true proportions regardless of distance; perspective creates vanishing points.

questions.question: In perspective projection, objects appear smaller as their distance from the viewer increases due to:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Perspective projection projects rays converging at a center of projection, causing distant objects to look smaller (foreshortening).

questions.question: Which hidden-surface elimination algorithm uses a depth buffer storing z-values for each pixel?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Z-buffer algorithm compares the depth (z-value) of each incoming fragment against the stored depth buffer value to keep the closest surface.

questions.question: Painter's algorithm eliminates hidden surfaces by:

options.B: Sorting polygons back to front by depth
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Painter's algorithm sorts surfaces from farthest to nearest (back-to-front) and draws them in order so nearer surfaces overwrite farther ones.

questions.question: Which shading model interpolates vertex intensities across a polygon rather than surface normals?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Gouraud shading computes lighting at vertices and linearly interpolates intensities; Phong shading interpolates normal vectors per pixel.

questions.question: Which of the following is an image-space hidden-surface removal method?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Z-buffer, Scan-line, and Warnock area-subdivision algorithms operate in image space (pixel/screen resolution). Back-face detection is object-space.

questions.question: Which color model is additive and primarily used for CRT/LCD display monitors?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: RGB (Red, Green, Blue) is an additive color model used by emissive displays; CMYK is subtractive and used for printing.

questions.question: In graphics, the jagged stair-step appearance along slanted raster lines is known as:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Aliasing (jaggies) occurs due to discrete pixel sampling of continuous edges; anti-aliasing smooths these transitions.

questions.question: Mapping a 2D coordinate window onto a screen display region is called:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The viewing transformation maps world-coordinate window contents onto the device-coordinate viewport.

questions.question: Which polygon clipping algorithm clips a polygon against each window boundary sequentially using four clippers?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Sutherland-Hodgman algorithm clips a polygon edge-by-edge sequentially against the Left, Right, Bottom, and Top window edges.

questions.question: How many control points define a standard cubic Bézier curve?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A cubic Bézier curve (degree 3) is defined by 4 control points (P0, P1, P2, P3). None of 2, 3, or 5 is correct.

questions.question: In Phong lighting/shading, which illumination components are combined?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Phong reflection model sums three components: ambient (background), diffuse (matte Lambertian), and specular (shiny highlights).

questions.question: The number of pixels per unit area or total horizontal by vertical pixel count of a display is called:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Resolution refers to the number of distinct pixels (e.g., 1920 × 1080) that can be displayed; aspect ratio is width-to-height proportion.

questions.question: In Java, which access specifier permits access within the same package AND to subclasses in other packages?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In Java, 'protected' grants access to all classes in the same package as well as subclasses in different packages.

questions.question: Which Java package contains the ArrayList collection class?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: ArrayList, HashMap, HashSet, and other Java Collections Framework classes reside in the java.util package.

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of Java's ArrayList compared to a standard array?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: ArrayList grows and shrinks dynamically at runtime and stores object references (primitives require wrapper classes like Integer).

questions.question: In Java exception handling, which statements about try, catch, and finally blocks are true?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three are true: try wraps code that may throw, catch handles matching exceptions, and finally executes cleanup code regardless of exceptions.

questions.question: Which Java keyword is used inside a method body to explicitly throw an exception object?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Java uses the 'throw' keyword to explicitly throw an exception instance inside a method; 'throws' declares checked exceptions in a signature.

questions.question: Which of the following is an unchecked exception (subclass of RuntimeException) in Java?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: NullPointerException extends RuntimeException (unchecked). IOException and SQLException are checked exceptions verified at compile time.

questions.question: What does JDBC stand for in Java?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: JDBC stands for Java Database Connectivity, the standard Java API for connecting and executing queries against relational databases.

questions.question: Which JDBC class establishes a Connection object using a database URL, username, and password?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, pass) selects an appropriate registered JDBC driver and returns a Connection object.

questions.question: In JDBC, which interface holds the tabular data returned by a SELECT SQL query?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Statement.executeQuery() returns a ResultSet object with a cursor to iterate row by row using next().

questions.question: Which JDBC Statement method executes INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE queries and returns the affected row count?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: executeUpdate() runs DML statements (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) and returns an int count of modified rows; executeQuery() is for SELECT.

questions.question: Which method in the Java Servlet lifecycle is called ONLY ONCE when the servlet is first loaded?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Servlet container calls init() once at initialization, service() for each incoming request, and destroy() once before unloading.

questions.question: Which sequence of methods defines the standard javax.servlet.Servlet lifecycle?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Servlet interface defines exactly three lifecycle methods: init() on load, service() per request, and destroy() before unloading.

questions.question: In Java Servlets, which method handles HTTP GET requests in HttpServlet?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: HttpServlet's service() dispatches HTTP GET requests to doGet(HttpServletRequest, HttpServletResponse) and POST to doPost().

questions.question: A JSP (JavaServer Pages) file is internally compiled by the container into a:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The JSP container translates a .jsp file into Java source code for a Servlet and compiles it into bytecode before execution.

questions.question: Which of the following are implicit objects available in JSP without explicit declaration?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: JSP provides 9 implicit objects including request, response, session, application, out, pageContext, config, page, and exception.

questions.question: In JSP syntax, which tag evaluates a Java expression and writes its result directly to the output stream?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: <%= expr %> is a JSP expression tag that outputs the evaluated value; <%! ... %> declares variables/methods; <%@ ... %> is a directive.

questions.question: What does XML stand for?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: XML stands for eXtensible Markup Language, a W3C standard for storing and transporting structured data using custom tags.

questions.question: When is an XML document considered 'well-formed'?

options.A: It validates against a CSS file
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A well-formed XML document follows XML syntax rules: single root element, proper nesting, closing tags, case sensitivity, and quoted attributes.

questions.question: What makes a 'valid' XML document different from merely a 'well-formed' XML document?

options.C: It conforms to a DTD or XSD
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A valid XML document is both well-formed AND conforms to the structure and rules defined in a DTD or XML Schema (XSD).

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE about XML tags?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In XML, tags are strictly case-sensitive, every non-empty tag must be closed, and there must be exactly ONE root element.

questions.question: In Java, which JDBC interface helps prevent SQL Injection by precompiling parameterized SQL queries?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: PreparedStatement precompiles SQL with '?' placeholders, separating SQL logic from user parameters and preventing SQL injection.

questions.question: In Java, which block is skipped ONLY if System.exit(0) is called or the JVM crashes?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The finally block always executes after try/catch (even on return statements), except when System.exit() terminates the JVM or a fatal error occurs.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid rule or feature of standard XML?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: XML uses custom user-defined tags, requires exactly one root element, and is strictly case-sensitive. All A, B, and C are false.

questions.question: Which method of Java's ArrayList inserts an element at the end of the list?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Java's ArrayList uses the add(E element) method to append an element to the end of the list, not pushBack(), append(), or insertLast().

questions.question: Which XML technology is used to define the valid structure and data types of an XML document?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Both DTD and XSD (XML Schema Definition) define valid XML structure and rules (XSD also adds rich data types). XSLT transforms XML.

questions.question: How does Dynamic Programming (DP) differ from the Greedy approach?

options.C: DP guarantees global optimum for optimal substructure
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three statements accurately contrast DP (memoization/tabulation of overlapping subproblems) with Greedy (irrevocable local choices).

questions.question: Which problem can be solved optimally by a Greedy algorithm?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Fractional Knapsack is solved greedily by sorting by value/weight ratio; 0/1 Knapsack and LCS require Dynamic Programming.

questions.question: Dijkstra's single-source shortest path algorithm fails to guarantee correctness when the graph contains:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Dijkstra's greedy relaxation assumes path distances never decrease when extended; negative-weight edges break this (use Bellman-Ford instead).

questions.question: What is the time complexity of Dijkstra's algorithm using a binary min-heap on a graph with V vertices and E edges?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Using an adjacency list and binary min-heap, Dijkstra performs at most V extract-min and E decrease-key operations, taking O((V + E) log V).

questions.question: Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms are both greedy algorithms used to find:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Both Prim's (vertex-growing) and Kruskal's (edge-sorting with Union-Find) compute a Minimum Spanning Tree of a weighted connected undirected graph.

questions.question: Which data structure does Kruskal's algorithm rely on to detect cycles efficiently?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Kruskal's algorithm sorts edges by weight and uses Disjoint Set Union (Find/Union) to skip edges whose endpoints are already connected.

questions.question: In a graph with n vertices, a Minimum Spanning Tree always contains how many edges?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Every spanning tree on n vertices is a connected acyclic subgraph and therefore has exactly n - 1 edges.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of the KMP (Knuth-Morris-Pratt) string matching algorithm for text length n and pattern length m?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: KMP precomputes the LPS (longest proper prefix-suffix) failure table in O(m) and scans the text without backtracking in O(n), totaling O(n + m).

questions.question: What does the LPS (failure function) array in KMP store for pattern index i?

options.A: Length of longest proper prefix that is also a suffix
options.B: Total character frequency in the pattern
options.C: Hash value of the substring up to index i
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: KMP's LPS array stores the length of the longest proper prefix of P[0..i] that is also a suffix of P[0..i], avoiding redundant comparisons.

questions.question: Which properties must hold for every valid Red-Black Tree?

options.B: No two adjacent red nodes exist
options.C: Equal black-height on all root-to-NIL paths
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All three are core Red-Black Tree invariants: black root, no red-red parent-child pair, and uniform black-height from any node to its descendant leaves.

questions.question: What is the worst-case height of a Red-Black Tree with n internal nodes?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A Red-Black Tree with n internal nodes has height h <= 2 log2(n + 1) = O(log n), guaranteeing logarithmic search, insert, and delete.

questions.question: According to the Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem, the maximum flow from source s to sink t equals:

options.A: Capacity of the maximum s-t cut
options.B: Capacity of the minimum s-t cut
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Ford and Fulkerson's Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem states that the maximum s-t flow value equals the minimum capacity among all s-t cuts.

questions.question: Which algorithm computes maximum flow in a flow network by repeatedly finding augmenting paths in a residual graph?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Ford-Fulkerson method (and Edmonds-Karp using BFS) increases flow along augmenting s-t paths in the residual graph until none remain.

questions.question: The Simplex algorithm is a classic optimization method used to solve:

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: George Dantzig's Simplex method solves Linear Programming problems by moving along vertices of the feasible convex polytope to optimize the objective.

questions.question: In the Simplex method for Linear Programming, an optimal solution (if finite) always occurs at:

options.A: The strict interior of the region
options.C: A vertex (corner point) of the feasible region
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: By the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Programming, if an optimal solution exists, at least one extreme point (vertex) of the feasible polytope is optimal.

questions.question: In a Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADC, how many clock cycles are needed to convert an n-bit digital output?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A Successive Approximation ADC performs binary search from MSB to LSB, requiring exactly n clock cycles for an n-bit conversion.

questions.question: Which property holds true for a Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADC?

options.A: Converts n bits in 1 clock cycle
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A SAR ADC uses 1 comparator, an internal DAC, and takes n clock cycles; Flash ADC uses 2^n - 1 comparators in 1 cycle.

questions.question: Why is the R/2R ladder DAC preferred over a binary-weighted resistor DAC for higher bit resolutions?

options.A: It requires only two resistor values (R and 2R)
options.C: It is easier to fabricate on ICs
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: An R/2R ladder uses only two resistor values (R and 2R), avoiding huge resistance spreads and simplifying integrated circuit fabrication.

questions.question: What is the resolution (step size) of an 8-bit DAC with a full-scale reference voltage of 5 V?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Step size (1 LSB) = V_ref / (2^n - 1) = 5 / 255 V ≈ 19.6 mV (full-scale output is V_ref × 255/256 if V_ref is full-scale step; standard formula uses 2^n - 1 = 255).

questions.question: Which type of Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) is the fastest, completing conversion in a single step?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A Flash ADC uses 2^n - 1 parallel comparators to convert an analog input in one step, making it the fastest ADC type.

questions.question: How many comparators does a 4-bit Flash ADC require?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: An n-bit Flash ADC requires 2^n - 1 comparators. For 4 bits, 2^4 - 1 = 15 comparators are needed.

questions.question: Which two key conditions are required for a problem to be solved effectively using Dynamic Programming?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Dynamic Programming applies when a problem exhibits both optimal substructure (A) and overlapping subproblems (B).

questions.question: In an R/2R ladder DAC with n bits, how many distinct resistor values are used?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Regardless of the bit count n, an R/2R ladder network uses only two resistance values: R and 2R.

questions.question: In the 0/1 Knapsack problem with n items and capacity W, what is the standard Dynamic Programming time complexity?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Filling the 2D DP table of size (n+1) × (W+1) takes O(n × W) pseudo-polynomial time and space (or O(W) space with 1D DP).

questions.question: Which algorithm solves All-Pairs Shortest Paths in O(V^3) time using Dynamic Programming?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Floyd-Warshall algorithm uses Dynamic Programming over intermediate vertices k = 1..V to find all-pairs shortest paths in O(V^3) time.
